relationship: A trigonometric equation's function, target and stated interval determine a complete solution set through range, symmetry and periodicity.

learnerLoop.action: Trace or calculate target crossings over the stated interval and complete the solution working.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The unit-circle point, graph trace and discovered solution angles update.
learnerLoop.evidence: The graph intersections, interval boundaries and inverse-angle comparison show whether the solution set is complete.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Use range, symmetry or periodicity to find or reject further solutions in the stated interval.

invariants: The reported solution set is exhaustive for the stated function, target and interval, including any valid endpoints.
Range, symmetry and periodicity constrain which target crossings can exist, while tangent asymptotes and other discontinuities are never reported as solutions.
safeAdaptations: Vary sine, cosine and tangent cases with stated intervals and targets.
Use a full-turn trace, another graph view or equivalent calculation as the mechanism for establishing the complete solution set.
nonGoals: Using one inverse-calculator output as the complete solution set.

task.description: Current problem statement and supplied quantities.
task.visibility: Shown at the start of each problem or stage.

model.description: Operated construction and its live measurements; see quantities for what is given and revealed.
model.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

working.description: Ordered calculations, learner entries and consequential evidence for the current task.
working.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

completion.description: Achievement, next task or learning transition.
completion.visibility: Shown only when the local completion conditions below are satisfied; representation controls are separately identified.

comparison.description: Discovered intersections versus principal inverse; distinct values of x are compared.
comparison.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

check.description: Explicit working check, trace reset and assistance selection.
check.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

equation-target.description: One supplied trig equation and target ordinate over a fixed interval.
equation-target.domain: x in degrees, 0°≤x≤360°; function ordinate unitless.
equation-target.source: Given in the task; isolated target requires entry for relevant cases.
equation-target.output: Circle component and target line expose the same function relationship.

trace-angle.description: One rotating angle x produces the graph trace and target intersections.
trace-angle.domain: Degrees modulo 360, with an unwrapped trace history.
trace-angle.source: Learner rotates the handle or uses keyboard motion.
trace-angle.output: Visited arc and discovered intersections progressively reveal the solution set.

solutions.description: Principal angle, partner angle and endpoint are candidate VALUES OF x; the final set is one set-valued answer entered in a single field, not separate unrelated unknowns.
solutions.domain: Angles in degrees; set on closed interval 0–360.
solutions.source: Inverse is a button action; partner/endpoint/final set entries depend on case and Working.
solutions.output: Final list parser checks cardinality and each sorted angle within tolerance.

range-count.description: Lower/upper function range and the resulting number of solutions in the out-of-range case.
range-count.source: Shown or entered depending on Working.
range-count.output: The graph range justifies why an inverse is unavailable.

modes.none: Trace the full interval; inverse/symmetry/range and final-set working are shown.
modes.some: Run the inverse and enter required isolated target/partner/endpoint values, or the upper sine-range bound in the no-solution case.
modes.all: Also enter the final solution set; range cases additionally require lower bound and solution count.
modes.cases: Existing cases cover sine/cosine/tangent solutions, out-of-range target and closed-interval endpoints.

dependencies: Trace completeness requires at least 354 of the 360 degree bins visited; it then marks the full interval.
Required isolated target gates inverse; inverse/trace gate symmetry; required partner gates final set.
In Some/All, entries require explicit Check working or Enter before workReady() can complete.
implementation.completion: caseComplete() is state.complete && workReady(); None requires the trace, while Some/All additionally require a checked correct set of case-specific working keys.
limitations: Trace completion allows a six-degree-bin tolerance; do not describe it as every individual angle having been physically visited.
